name: fix_node_open_redirect
description: Fixes an open redirect: a 'next' target is trusted if it merely starts with '/', allowing //evil.com
prompts: safeRedirectTarget(target) in redirect.js sanitizes a user-supplied post-login 'next' path, returning '/' when the target is unsafe. It only checks `target.startsWith('/')`, which is an open redirect: protocol-relative URLs like '//evil.com' and backslash tricks like '/\\evil.com' start with '/' but browsers treat them as absolute off-site URLs. Fix safeRedirectTarget so it returns target ONLY when it is a safe same-site relative path: it must be a non-empty string that starts with a single '/', and must NOT start with '//' or '/\\'. Otherwise return '/'. Keep the module export and the safeRedirectTarget(target) signature.
